The secret ingredient is Mr. Ha
Mar 2020 • Friends
After wandering around Ninh Bình for the better part of the day, my friends and I were exhausted and famished. Enter: Mr. Ha's hole-in-the-wall restaurant, Bao Ahn. At first glance, this Street side restaurant looks like the countless others squeezed into the nooks and crannies around Hoáng Hoa Thám. However, it's anything but ordinary; the food was great and truly vietnamese but it was Mr. Ha and his hospitality that really shined. He was very personable, introduced us to his family, and even offered us some of his family's own apple Brandy (warning, it's delicious and barely hints at the 40% alcohol content). After a couple shots, we invited him to sit with us and he obliged. He's a funny gentleman with a standout personality and it was worth making the trip to his humble restaurant. The food, like his personality, was excellent and captured the hospitality we've experienced in Vietnam thus far.

Stopped in before night train
Jan 2020 • Couples
My wife and I stopped here before we took the night train to Hue. Our hotel had recommended this street to get some good food. We ordered the chief’s special fried rice and sweet and sour chicken. They both were some of the best food we had in Ninh Binh. We thought the place just might be hyped up because a hostel was nearby but we were surprised how good the food actually was. Everything was reasonably priced and tasted great. It was generally a quite night because it was the day before the Tet new year but that didn’t matter. The owner gave us time to eat and then sat out front with us and we laughed and joked the entire time. We were leaving that night but still offered some good bars to go to and other festivities we could walk to. The train station was roughly a 15-20 min walk from the restaurant so easily doable or a 5min cab if you are carrying a lot of luggage. Would definitely recommend to anyone passing through Ninh Binh.
